submitter: bugfix_357_component_identity lane — a page_components row's identity, bytes and content_data are written and carried as one bundle and no seam asserts they agree. 22 live rows name the shared `hero` component while storing a whole interactive tool; newest born 2026-08-22 on a site homepage. Successor to bugs_closed/277, whose lane's closing handoff routed here.
rationale:
A tool/game page's HTML is one `<div class="tool-page">` fragment with no `<section>` element. saveSectionsExtractFromHTML's documented fallback stores it as ONE section named "section" — the sentinel meaning IDENTITY UNKNOWN. enrichSectionsWithPlannedNames then replaces that sentinel with planned[Position-1] read from pages.sections, and `hero` is planned first on all 22 affected pages, so the tool is named `hero` purely by position. enrichSectionsWithComponentIDs resolves the name to the shared hero UUID and the single INSERT persists slot_name='hero' + component_id=<hero> + rendered_html=<the whole tool>. The sentinel for 'I do not know what this is' is converted into a confident wrong answer.

It is NOT historical: the writer is settled by row fingerprint (all 22 carry content_brief.section_guidance='hero section' and position=1, and save_page_sections_action.go is the only page_components writer that writes content_brief at all), and the newest row was created 2026-08-22 08:50:12 on vetcomparison.uk's HOMEPAGE, which now serves `class="tool-page"` where its hero should be and `data-component="hero"` zero times.

And it is self-renewing, which is why this is a flow fix and not a data repair. RerenderPageSectionsAction renders a fresh hero title band for the hero slot; the save's Layer 2 interactive carry-forward then detects that the stored row for that slot is interactive while the incoming content is not, and splices the STORED TOOL BYTES and STORED hero content_data back into the section that still carries the hero identity (save_page_sections_action.go:522-535, whose own comment says 'e.g. the hero regenerated as plain text'). The mechanism that PROTECTS the tool from being blanked is the same mechanism that PERPETUATES the mislabelling. Measured: vetcomparison.uk index has six completed rerenders 08-19..08-22 and the tool serves throughout; its rows were re-created INSIDE the 08:44:51->08:50:19 window.

I want to record a retraction, because it changes the shape of the fix. I first claimed the 13 rows carrying a full hero content_data were 'already armed' — one rebuild from having the tool replaced by a title band. That is REFUTED by the six rerenders above and is logged in WRONG_CALLS.md. Nothing here rests on it.

The discriminator is measured, not guessed. 357's own fix candidate 2 warns a birth guard must be censused first because the static-template-prefix test also fires on legitimate template drift: it flags 158 rows fleet-wide and is unusable at a refusal seam. Testing the component's OWN self-declaration instead — the data-component attribute, which saveSectionsExtractFromHTML already trusts as the identity carrier in this same file — gives 1,550 rows agreeing, 0 both-declared disagreements, and 27 flagged. The 1,550 agreements are the demand control: the predicate could have come out otherwise and did, 1,550 times. Of the 27, THREE are legitimate (loancash.co.uk verbatim pages: rebuild_policy='owned', exactly one component row, content_data->>'deploy_mode'='verbatim' — they store a full document because that is what a verbatim page IS), so the guard carries a verbatim exemption and the genuine set is 24. I originally reported 'zero false positives' having not opened those rows; that is corrected here and logged.

plan.summary: ROUND 2 — RESIZED, and the resizing is the substance. Round 1 bundled a change to what the save PERSISTS (Layer A: typing the no-<section> fallback row) with the verification (Layer B/D). While answering the bug_historian's gating objection I found a defect in my own round-1 plan that is worse than the objection: the Layer 2 interactive carry-forward matches stored rows to incoming ones SOLELY by slot-name equality (save_page_sections_action.go:517), so renaming a slot to 'adopted-fragment' makes the next plan-driven rebuild miss the match and take the 'default:' re-append branch — the incoming hero title band is saved AND the tool is appended beside it. My 'byte-preserving' change would have altered what 22 live pages serve. So Layer A, the component seed and the stock repair are WITHDRAWN from this round. What remains changes NO persisted output at all: verify identity against the bytes at the single INSERT and RECORD it (Error level, deduped work item, refusal behind an opt-in field seeded on nobody), detect the class fleet-wide across all six writers, register the concept, and pin the slot-matching behaviour with a test so the deferred half cannot be built blind.

edits.rationale: The verification, at the seam. For each section with a resolved ComponentID, compare the component template's data-component value against the one in the section's HTML and flag when the template declares one and the HTML's value IS DISTINCT FROM it (absence counts — that is the whole pathological class, and `<>` returns a clean zero here because NULL is not false; the trap is in the lane RUNBOOK). NO verbatim exemption at this seam, and that is a reachability argument rather than an omission: a verbatim page is rebuild_policy='owned' by definition of the triple, and the owned-page guard at save_page_sections_action.go:186 refuses the whole save unconditionally, before every section-level guard (VERIFIED — a bare block immediately after the page lookup, whose own comment says it refuses 'rather than fall through to the heuristic guards below'). A copied-in exemption clause here would be dead code inviting a later reader to delete the real protection. The DETECTOR (edit 5) carries the exemption explicitly instead, sharing the canonical triple with loadVerbatimPageHTML rather than respelling it. REUSE, NOT ADDITION, on 342's pattern (and the reuse_agent seat's round-1 objection is right that the consolidation only counts if the EXISTING sites are repointed — they are, in this same edit, and the round-2 verification asserts zero remaining inline compilations): the data-component extraction this whole plan rests on is already compiled inline TWICE in save_page_sections_action.go (:1392 and :1498, identical regex), and the guard plus detector would make four spellings in two languages — while the spellings must differ subtly (HTML side `[^"]+`, template side `[^"{]+`, so an interpolated attribute never counts as a declaration). One helper pair replaces both inline compilations and is used by the extractor, the enricher and the guard, with the SQL rendering generated from the same source on the interactiveHTMLSQL 'ONE definition, two languages' precedent (:1695-1710) and its parity test. Otherwise the enricher could adopt an identity the guard then refuses on a different reading of the same attribute. Report level is Error, by 342's own reasoning: Warn is the siblings' level for degraded-but-legitimate (a merely-empty optional field), Error for definitionally wrong (a dead URL control). Refuse-on-certainty only: the 190 of 339 components declaring no data-component are invisible to it, stated as a limit in the file rather than glossed.

Placement is the one thing this must not copy from its precedent. sectionIsUnresolvableStub skips inside the insert loop, AFTER the DELETE — correct for a hollow stub, because nothing of value is lost. Here the row holds the ONLY copy of a tool, so a post-DELETE skip would empty the page. The call therefore runs BEFORE the history snapshot and the DELETE, beside the claims/shrink/floor guards, honouring this file's own stated doctrine that 'a refused save writes nothing at all'. It runs AFTER the Layer 2 interactive carry-forward so it judges the FINAL bytes — which is precisely what breaks the conservation loop once armed, because the re-spliced hero-identity/tool-bytes section arrives at the seam already self-contradictory.

The seam guard only sees rows flowing through save_page_sections. Five other writers insert page_components (deploy_tool_action, create_tool_component_action, create_report_page_action, rebuild_blog_listing_action, adopt_verbatim) and this covers their output without touching any of them — the alternative being five edits that each depend on the author remembering. Files the SAME component_identity_mismatch item type as the seam; two producers of one type is blessed by the 2026-08-02 owner ruling provided the register entry names the producer set and the item_key shape, which it does. No automated repair route is wired, deliberately: auto-repairing identity is exactly the destructive-fix class bugs_closed/277 was nearly destroyed by. The seam and the detector deliberately ask DIFFERENT questions and their divergence is signal, stated at both sites so nobody 'fixes' one to match the other: the seam asks 'could the component I am about to bind have produced the bytes I am about to store?' (final post-carry-forward bytes, templates as at write time); the detector asks 'does this stored row still agree with its component's CURRENT self-declaration?' (rows at rest, templates as they are today). They legitimately diverge on template drift — a row written when the two agreed and flagged after the template's attribute changed is a STALE ROW, not a detector bug, and drift being the detector's legitimate secondary catch is the same property that made the static-prefix test wrong for the SEAM. ITEM_KEY IS ONE CONSTANT, not two string templates (reuse_agent round-1): the seam and the detector both call componentIdentityItemKey(domain, page, slot) from the guard file, so the dedup key cannot drift between the two producers.

Condition (2) of the platform-seams ruling, in the SAME commit that ships the seam. Records: the adopted-fragment component and its known limit (its {{.body}} template declares no data-component, so the Layer B guard can never vouch for the rows it types — accepted, because the alternative wraps the fragment in a <section data-component=...> and changes served bytes on live pages); the component_identity_mismatch item type with BOTH producers named and the item_key shape stated (2026-08-02 ruling 1); and the opt-in field with its default and the fact that nothing seeds it. ROUND-2 CORRECTION, and the tooling_provenance seat was right: this edit will NOT hand-edit the index headline count. LANDMINES records that stored counts in 000_concept_index.md have been RETIRED — the checker reads only the first 4,000 bytes (STORED_COUNT_HEAD_BYTES) and its own line says 'any that reappears is the finding', so writing a fresh accurate count is not compliance, it fires the drift check daily. CLAUDE.md's 'update the index count' instruction is the anti-pattern here. The entry row is added; the count line is left alone; the two-way comm parity check (entries with no index row, index rows with no entry) is run instead.

edits.rationale: The half that matters is the silence. Tests: (a) a hero-typed tool-bytes section is flagged; (b) a legitimate verbatim single-row page is NOT flagged (the loancash case, which the first version of this predicate got wrong); (c) a component whose template interpolates its own attribute is NOT flagged; (d) a component declaring no data-component is NOT flagged; (e) with the field OFF the save PROCEEDS and the item is still filed; (f) with the field ON the save is refused and the page's rows are UNCHANGED — asserted by row count AND per-row md5 before/after, because a refusal that has already run the DELETE is the exact placement bug this design varies its precedent to avoid, and a mock's own bookkeeping cannot assert that negative. ROUND 2 adds the test that the deferred half most needs: TestLayer2MatchingIsSlotNameOnly pins that the interactive carry-forward matches solely on sections[i].ComponentName == p.slot (:517), so that the day someone renames a slot the failure is a named test rather than a live page gaining a hero band.

plan.risks:
WHAT CHANGED SINCE ROUND 1, stated first because it is the point. Three of the round-1 edits are withdrawn — the fallback typing (Layer A), the adopted-fragment seed, and the positional-enrichment narrowing — for a reason I found while checking the gating objection rather than while defending it. bug_historian asked whether the honest-unknown degrade path had been tested against the Layer 2 carry-forward. Its stated mechanism is wrong — Layer 2's PROTECTION keys purely on the bytes (interactiveHTMLSQL / sectionHTMLIsInteractive are ILIKE and strings.Contains over rendered_html, never component_id or template) — but the question was the right one, because Layer 2's MATCHING is `sections[i].ComponentName == p.slot` and nothing else. Rename the slot and the match fails, the 'default:' branch re-appends the tool, and the incoming hero band is saved beside it. That is a change to what four live sites serve, arriving as a side effect of a change I described as byte-preserving. It needs pages.sections updated in the same transaction, or identity-agnostic matching, and either is its own round with its own measurement.

OBJECTIONS ANSWERED BY CHECKING, not by argument:
- prior_art (dormant machinery): no existing component is a byte-preserving passthrough. `SELECT name FROM content_components WHERE regexp_replace(html_template,'\s','','g') ~ '^\{\{\.?[A-Za-z_]+\}\}$'` returns ZERO rows. The gap is genuine — but the component is deferred with Layer A regardless.
- prior_art + reuse_agent (is the duplication real?): YES, verified — `dataComponentRe := regexp.MustCompile(`data-component="([^"]+)"`)` at :1392 AND :1498, byte-identical, used at :1427, :1463 and :1509. Both are deleted and repointed in edit 1; the parity precedent interactiveHTMLSQL (:1698-1710) has its test in interactivity_guard_test.go.
- editquality (ON CONFLICT idempotency): a UNIQUE index DOES exist — content_components_name_key on (name) — so ON CONFLICT (name) is sound. Recorded for the deferred seed round rather than used here.
- architecture (declare the optional-key count before adding the Nth key): the honest answer is that it CANNOT be read, and that is itself the finding. `scripts/audit-optional-key-budget.sh --json` audits 123 actions against budget N=10 and lists 99 more as `uncounted` — **save_page_sections is in the uncounted list**, because it has no RegisterActionInputSpec. So this new key enters counted as ZERO: precisely the retract_asset_files/publish_site trap CLAUDE.md names. I am not asserting it is under budget; I am reporting that the instrument cannot see this action at all, and edit 1 therefore declares a spec rather than adding an invisible key.
- tooling_provenance (the index count): correct, and the register edit no longer touches the headline. Stored counts are RETIRED; the checker reads the first 4,000 bytes and 'any that reappears is the finding'.
- bug_historian (Layer D is detection-only at five other writers): accepted and named as RESIDUAL EXPOSURE, not as closed. The mechanism stays live and unrefused at deploy_tool_action, create_tool_component_action, create_report_page_action, rebuild_blog_listing_action and adopt_verbatim; what this round buys is that it becomes VISIBLE there, which is the precondition for deciding anything about it.

STILL TRUE FROM ROUND 1: the guard records at the seam and refuses nothing on roll (the field is seeded on nobody), which is 342's shipped behaviour and its own stated next step. The refuse-on-certainty limit stands — 190 of 339 components declare no data-component and the guard says nothing about them. And I flag against my own interest, again, that the sibling opt-in from RFC_010's worked example is named by ZERO live configs: if the council reads that as evidence this estate does not come back to arm default-OFF switches, say so and I will drop the refusal arm rather than add another inert key.
